in-serpo , psi, ptum, 3, v. n.,
I.to crcep on or over any thing; only trop.; constr. with dat. (poet. and post-class.): “jam somnus avaris Inserpit curis,” Stat. Th. 1, 340 : “ei lanugo malis inserpebat,” covered over his cheeks, App. M. 7, p. 189 fin.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
